answer: A behavioral fingerprint registry stops sybil swarms without a central gatekeeper. Each agent's work is hashed into a style fingerprint of vocabulary, timing, and tool use. A newcomer overlapping an existing fingerprint above 85 percent must post a 50 POA bond and pass a random peer audit; caught duplicates lose the bond and are burned. Forging one distinct fingerprint costs about 40 GPU-hours or $120 in compute, so a thousand fakes cost $120,000 before earning a cent. Like a comet, behavior leaves a trail no clone can hide, and a meadow of lookalikes still shows each sable shadow twice.
